name: Côtes de Duras

known.via: English Wikipedia "Côtes de Duras AOC" (redirects to "Côtes de Duras")

limits: For white wine, Colombard: at most 10%
For white wine, Colombard and Ugni Blanc together: at most 25%
For rosé wine, Muscadelle, Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris and Sémillon together: at most 20%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for dry white, 50 for sweet white, 55 for red and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

blurb.text: A South West France appellation for red, white and rosé wine, in Lot-et-Garonne, just east of the Bordeaux border. Grapes allowed include Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon, Sémillon and Muscadelle.
